newsitem.title: USA: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates fall 4th wk in row.
newsitem.headline: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates fall 4th wk in row.

text.p: Average commitment rates on U.S. 30- and 15-year fixed-rate mortgages fell a fourth consecutive week during the week ending June 27, Freddie Mac said Thursday.

Thirty-year mortgages fell three basis points in the week to an average 7.58 percent from 7.61 percent. Freddie Mac said the 30-year has not been lower since it stood at 7.56 percent in the week ended February 21, 1997.
Fifteen-year mortgages inched down to an average 7.13 percent from 7.14 percent, the lowest since a rate of 7.06 percent also in the February 21 week.
One-year adjustable rate mortgages were unchanged at 5.66 percent in the week. The ARM has not been lower since it stood at 5.61 percent in the week ended March 14, 1997, Freddie Mac said.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 8.29 percent, the 15-year 7.82 percent and the ARM 5.98 percent.

"The market continues to feel that inflation is no threat at the present time and that the Federal Reserve will take little, if any, action when it meets in July," Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist, said in a statement.
"Thus, interest rates remain affordably low right now, though they may inch back up a bit next week," Van Order added.
Lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.5 percent on ARM loans, also unchanged from the previous week.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
